To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured the permittivity, propagation loss, and reflection coefficient of concrete, mortar, and various corrosion samples.

1) coarse aggregate reduces the electromagnetic propagation loss through concrete; 2) corrosion sample spectra are very similar to magnetite; 3) corrosion sample spectra have a prominent peak between 1 GHz and 2.2 GHz; and 4) the corrosion sample spectra are consistent with a mixture of magnetite and hematite.
the electromagnetic spectra of corrosion samples are similar to the spectra of iron oxide samples, and that coarse aggregate reduces the electromagnetic propagation loss through concrete.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electromagnetic properties of iron oxides and the dielectric and propagation loss of corrosion in concrete.
identifying electromagnetic signatures that are both consistent with corrosion and prominent within concrete.
the development of nondestructive techniques for the evaluation of corrosion of steel rebar in concrete.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the electromagnetic spectra of corrosion samples and magnetite are similar and that the spectra of the corrosion sample and magnetite are both similar and distinct from the spectra of the concrete samples.
the permittivity of concrete varies with moisture and temperature, but that the propagation loss is relatively constant and that the magnetic susceptibility is negligible.
our measurements are consistent with the hypothesis that the dielectric and/or magnetic features of corrosion products may be useful for quantifying rebar within concrete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electromagnetic spectra of iron oxides and rebar corrosion samples are similar, with features between 0.1 GHz to 10 GHz that could be useful for quantifying rebar and other corrosion in concrete.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of electromagnetic metrology to quantify rebar corrosion within concrete structures.
the permittivity of concrete can be measured using a waveguide and the propagation loss is affected by the coarse aggregate.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dielectric constant and propagation loss of concrete are strongly dependent on the type of aggregate, while the dielectric constant of iron oxide powders are similar to those from corrosion samples, and that both have a feature between 500 MHz and 2 GHz.
there are features in the dielectrics of iron-oxides and corrosion samples that are consistent across the frequency range from 50 MHz to 50GHz.
the electromagnetic spectrum can be a useful tool for identifying and quantifying corrosion.
